title: Arc fit
tagline: Turn freeform coplanar edges into a chain of lines and circular arcs within a position tolerance -- for CAM and for radius callouts.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Machines and drawings want lines and arcs; design curves are splines. Arc fit replaces each edge with the fewest lines and arcs that stay within tolerance, keeping edges that already are arcs or lines.
useWhen: A spline sidecut needs radius callouts
slides.caption: AR3: a spline S-curve -> 10 arcs within 0.008 mm.

points.head: Keep what is exact
points.body: An edge that already is a circle or line passes through whole.

points.head: Biarcs
points.body: Each segment: a line, a biarc (two tangent arcs matching the end tangents) or a 3-point arc.

points.head: Split, then merge
points.body: Split at the worst point until in tolerance; merge neighbours while it stays in tolerance.

slides.title: The dialog
params: Coplanar edges, selected in chain order.
Largest deviation (0.01 mm); also the join tolerance.

slides.title: Example: AR3
slides.head: A spline S-curve (R14 core into an R3 reverse flank), tolerance 0.01 mm
slides.body: 10 arcs, within 0.008 mm both ways, one wire. Also tested: AR1 five exact arcs pass through unchanged; AR2 a spline on an R14 arc -> one arc R14000; AR4 2 mm knot spans with a 10 mm minimum -> no gaps.

keys: The arc-fit wire (empty when Output type is Sketch).
messages: Raise Plane tolerance or fix the input.

items.head: Order matters
items.body: Select the edges in chain order; they are not re-ordered.

items.head: Across edges
items.body: Arcs are tangent within an input edge, not across input edges.

items.head: Tight tolerances
items.body: Very small tolerances drive every segment to maximum depth: slow.
